organizations.normalization_notes: The 1940 historical name and author-affiliation wording are preserved. The record does not substitute a modern successor or establish the exact legal employment relationship.

affiliations.date_precision: The author affiliation was published 1940-01-01; start and end dates are not stated.
affiliations.research_notes: ASTM's contemporary publisher record explicitly gives The Pure Oil Co. as Chittick's author affiliation. It does not state his role, formal employment terms, or the date and route of his later OSS association, so the project does not label it the immediate affiliation or last civilian employer.

affiliations.date_precision: Observation recorded 1944-02-08; actual work dates and relation to OSS entry are unestablished.
affiliations.research_notes: No named employer, workplace, employment dates, immediate pre-OSS affiliation or last civilian employer is established. The dated Army observation is not converted into an employer claim.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Colonel Martin B Chittick is a high-confidence match to the Chemical Warfare Service officer and technical author.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The 1943 Official Register names Colonel Martin B. Chittick as deputy chief of the Chemical Warfare Service Technical Division, while the 1940 ASTM record identifies the same distinctive name with The Pure Oil Co.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact, distinctive full name and colonel rank connect the index to the official wartime register; the earlier technical subject and Chicago company affiliation supply coherent but not independently identifier-backed continuity.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official register observes a wartime military assignment in May 1943 but does not establish the date or sequence of Chittick's OSS association.
claims.match_notes: The six-digit number printed in the OSS index is preserved and was not padded for comparison with the Army bulk file.

claims.claim_text: In 1940, Martin B. Chittick was professionally affiliated with The Pure Oil Co. in Chicago.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Chittick, Martin, B. The Pure Oil Co., Chicago, Ill.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: ASTM's publisher record gives The Pure Oil Co. in Chicago as Chittick's author affiliation for a paper published in 1940.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence match based on the exact distinctive full name, technical subject continuity and the matching colonel named in the 1943 Official Register and OSS index.
claims.temporal_assessment: The affiliation is explicitly dated by the 1940 publication and therefore predates OSS; neither its exact duration nor its proximity to Chittick's OSS association is shown.
claims.match_notes: Published as a professional institutional affiliation, not silently converted into a verified employer, immediate affiliation or last civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: A probable source match identifies T/5 Ernest L. Chmieleski among OSS personnel in Yugoslavia.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: An institutional historical article lists T/5 Ernest L. Chmieleski, with a bracketed spelling variant, among OSS personnel in Yugoslavia and describes their 1944 operations.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact full name and middle initial are distinctive and occur in matching OSS context, but no private identifier or personnel-file bridge independently confirms the match.
claims.temporal_assessment: The article concerns OSS service from April through June 1944 and supplies no pre-OSS employer or recruitment chronology.
claims.match_notes: The source's bracketed alternative spelling remains evidence context and is not adopted as an index correction without archival confirmation.

claims.claim_text: A probable source match identifies T/5 Joseph Chochola among OSS personnel in Yugoslavia.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: An institutional historical article lists T/5 Joseph Chochola among OSS personnel in Yugoslavia and describes the group's 1944 operations.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The uncommon first name and surname occur in matching OSS context, but the article omits the index middle initial and supplies no private identifier or personnel-file bridge.
claims.temporal_assessment: The article concerns OSS service from April through June 1944 and supplies no pre-OSS employer or recruitment chronology.
claims.match_notes: Published only as a qualified probable identity; the archival file is still required to confirm it.

claims.claim_text: DeForest D Choha has an identifier-backed Army record match.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The private identifier matches an Army entry whose spaced name is the exact indexed name and whose February 1944 grade is private first class.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact indexed name and private identifier; identity assessed high confidence.
claims.temporal_assessment: The dated Army observation does not by itself establish an employer, OSS entry date or later OSS role.
claims.match_notes: The private identifier is masked publicly. The printed index value and spelling remain unchanged.

claims.claim_text: The Army entry records the occupational group ‘Mechanics and repairmen, airplane.’
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact private-identifier Army record carries code 580, which the inspected applicable NARA code sheet labels Mechanics and repairmen, airplane.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Exact indexed name and private identifier; identity assessed high confidence.
claims.temporal_assessment: Observed 1944-02-08; temporal relationship to OSS entry remains uncertain.
claims.match_notes: No employer is named and no employment date is inferred.
